title: Book Two · Chapter 198: Four at the River
story:
Early summer brings a free afternoon. Ronan, Leo, Mei, and Jun take a ball and a little food to the open space near the river.

Mei has two boiled eggs in a cloth. Jun has a packet of crackers. Leo brings water. Ronan carries four small cups in his bag.

“Very fine cups,” Leo says. “Do they have all their handles?”

“They have no handles.”

“Nothing missing, then.”

They find a dry place under a tree. The ball stays on the open square, away from the river fence. They play two against two. At first, Ronan and Jun stand on the same side.

Ronan feels a small hope. Jun throws the ball to him and calls for it back. They pass it three times. Then Leo takes it.

They are playing a game. Ronan lets it stay a game.

After a while, the game stops. They change teams. Mei scores twice. Leo looks down and tells his feet to move faster. Jun says Leo's feet should choose their own rules.

They stop when everyone is too warm. Ronan pours water into the cups. Mei breaks the eggs in half. One half has much more yellow than the other. She keeps that half for herself.

“Honest work,” Leo says.

“I brought them,” she answers.

They eat and watch the river. Jun takes out a small drawing book. He draws Leo's shoe first. The shoe looks longer on the page than it does on the ground.

“Room for the chair inside it,” Ronan says.

Leo explains the chair joke to Mei and Jun. They laugh until he tells them the real chair will stay at home.

The afternoon grows quieter after that. Leo talks about leaving near the end of summer. Mei wants to know about the new school's reading room. Jun asks if the bedroom has good light.

No one tells Leo to give up the plan.

Before they pack, Ronan asks Jun about a small drawing for his own reading notes. Jun looks at the book in Ronan's hand.

“I can show you a simple way,” he says. “I do not want to join a new project.”

“That is all right.”

Jun draws two easy lines and gives the pencil back. Ronan tries them himself. His first shape is poor. The second is better.

On the way home, they carry their own rubbish. Leo has the empty egg cloth because Mei's hands are full. Ronan carries the cups, all four together.

At the turn, Jun and Mei go one way. Leo goes another. Ronan walks to the green door with grass on one shoe. He takes the shoe off outside. Mum sees the sock underneath and laughs. Ronan carries both shoes inside.
studyGuide:
## 词句提示

boiled＝煮熟的；cracker＝薄脆饼干；pass＝传球；rubbish＝垃圾。

## 理解问题

1. Ronan怎样享受和Jun打球，而不把它当成完全恢复搭档的证明？
2. Jun在画画帮助上给出了什么有限而明确的答复？

## 读句子

**They change teams.**

拆开看：They / change / teams.

他们／交换／队伍。
